feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report whether the signal is smooth across the span with the 16 mm footprint (any saturation at the edges or a dead zone at centre?). Say whether the new y = 0.03 lookahead reduced overshoot or lag compared with the earlier 0.05 row. Say whether the narrower 0.10 m track gave enough turn authority, or whether the robot now turns too sharply and oscillates. Say whether the outer sensors at plus or minus 0.04 m are doing useful work.

intent: Test whether lookahead lag and footprint size caused the early line loss. Sensors move back to y = 0.03 and enlarge to 16 mm; wheel_track narrows to 0.10 m for more turn authority. Span, wheel radius, body and mass stay fixed. Expected: line_loss_events fall toward 0, max_error drops below the 0.06 m off-track limit, and progress extends past the first bend.
learning: The baseline lost the line early on every track with max_error near the 0.06 m off-track limit. Compare the next race against iteration 0 on line_loss_events and max_error first. If line losses drop but the robot still drifts off on bends, widen the outer sensors toward plus or minus 0.06 m. If steering oscillates, move the row back toward y = 0.02 and keep the 16 mm footprint.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced nothing yet. The only evidence is the development-simulator summary for the baseline geometry. All 60 trials went off track, with none finished. Mean progress was 0.04 to 0.115, and max_error sat at about 0.06 to 0.069, just past the 0.06 m off-track floor. Every run logged one line-loss event and never recovered. The robot loses the line early and drifts off, rather than oscillating: steering_oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.15). The sensor array should still cover the tape, since 5 sensors at 2 cm spacing with 12 mm footprints overlap across the whole band. So the failure is more likely lag or too little steering authority than a gap in coverage. Three geometry levers address this. (1) Move the sensor row back to y = 0.03 from 0.05. The 5 cm lookahead means the controller reacts to the line about 5 cm before the wheels reach it. At speed that delay lets the robot overshoot the bend, and it is the lag my earlier feedback flagged. (2) Set sensor_size to 0.016. A larger footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape at once, so the line stays visible through the bend and a loss is less likely. (3) Narrow wheel_track to 0.10 m. Turn rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by track, so a narrower track gives more yaw per unit of PWM steering. This should help the robot follow tighter bends. I keep the sensor span at plus or minus 0.04 m, the body, the mass, and the wheel radius, so the next race tests the sensing and track change without confounding it. I expect fewer line-loss events, lower max_error, and progress past the first bend. Scores should rise only if the robot then completes the course, so I am not expecting a finish yet.
